description: Ninth-round conservative temporal backfill candidates for remaining non-CN/non-CA clean research_temporal_dates rows. This report is research-only and is not merged into temporal overrides.
scope_notes: Manual-classification, nonstandard, and possible overlay-artifact rows were excluded.
Included source_ids were checked against webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_base_temporal_overrides.json and were not present there at generation time.
Where no public establishment date was found, start_year is a conservative documented-by operational year, not an inferred construction year.

candidates.name: Kirtland, Kirtland Air Force Base Auxiliary Field

source_notes.title: Kirtland Air Force Base > Base History
source_notes.note: Official Kirtland history describes Army transfer and conversion of the Albuquerque/Oxnard aviation facilities in 1941-1942.

source_notes.title: Kirtland Air Force Base
source_notes.note: The base article lists Kirtland AFB as built in 1941 and used from 1942 to present, with auxiliary airfields used for wartime flying-school support.

candidates.rationale: The queue row is an auxiliary-field variant tied to Kirtland AFB. The 1941 start is a conservative facility-start year for the wartime military airfield complex rather than a separately proven auxiliary-strip opening date.

candidates.name: Deversoir Station

source_notes.title: Data and Station Information for DEVERSOIR - PSMSL
source_notes.note: PSMSL lists the Deversoir station in Egypt with a data time span of 1937-1941.

source_notes.note: The Abu Sultan/RAF Deversoir article identifies Deversoir as a RAF military airfield built in the 1930s and handed to the Egyptian Air Force in 1955.

candidates.rationale: The GeoNames row is a Deversoir coast/signal station rather than the air base itself. The 1937 start is included only as conservative documented station presence near the historically military Deversoir area; no closure is asserted for the station feature.

candidates.name: Puerto Belgrano Naval Air Base

source_notes.title: 82 anos de la Base Aeronaval Comandante Espora - Argentina.gob.ar
source_notes.note: The Argentine Navy article states construction began in 1936 and the base was officially inaugurated on 16 June 1939; early names included Base Aeronaval de Puerto Belgrano.

source_notes.title: Base Aeronaval Comandante Espora
source_notes.note: The base article records 1936-1939 construction and official inauguration on 16 June 1939, with Puerto Belgrano among the earlier names.

candidates.rationale: The queue row name aligns with an early name of what became Base Aeronaval Comandante Espora. The 1939 start is the official inauguration year; no sourced closure was found.

source_notes.title: Base Naval Ushuaia - Moovit
source_notes.note: The transit/location entry summarizes the base as founded on 13 December 1950 for support ships operating in the southern sector.

candidates.rationale: The 1950 date is direct founding evidence for the named naval base, with no sourced closure.

candidates.name: Base Aeronaval Punta Indio

source_notes.title: Base Aeronaval Punta Indio
source_notes.note: The Spanish article states that Base Aeronaval Punta Indio was inaugurated at the beginning of 1925 and remained a naval aviation base in 2025.

source_notes.title: Punta Indio Naval Air Base
source_notes.note: The English article states Punta Indio Naval Air Base was established in 1928, reflecting a more conservative alternate establishment year.

candidates.rationale: Sources differ between an early-1925 inauguration and 1928 establishment language. The candidate uses 1925 because it is direct Spanish-language inauguration evidence and leaves the endpoint open.

candidates.name: Vlore Air Base

source_notes.title: Vlore Air Base
source_notes.note: The air-base article states that Vlore Air Base was constructed in the 1950s, that the Air Academy was established in 1962, and that the air base was destroyed during the 1997 lottery uprising.

source_notes.title: Vlore Air Base - AirportDatabase.net
source_notes.note: AirportDatabase identifies Vlore Air Base/LAVL in Albania with runway and location details.

candidates.rationale: The 1950 start is decade-level construction evidence represented as the earliest year of the 1950s. The 1997 endpoint is supported as destruction of the air base, though later directory entries still preserve the airport code/location.
